ch9.title: Muscles and Muscle Tissue
ch9.status: current — mish is on this NOW

muscle_tissue_types.skeletal: voluntary, striated, multinucleated. attached to bones via tendons. conscious control.
muscle_tissue_types.cardiac: involuntary, striated, branched, intercalated discs. autorhythmic. heart only.
muscle_tissue_types.smooth: involuntary, non-striated, spindle-shaped. walls of hollow organs, blood vessels, airways.

skeletal_muscle_structure.organization: muscle → fascicle → muscle fiber → myofibril → sarcomere
skeletal_muscle_structure.note: epi = on top, peri = around, endo = within. same prefix logic as endosteum/periosteum from bones.

sarcomere.what: functional unit of contraction. Z-line to Z-line.

bands.A_band: dark band. length of myosin (thick filaments). does NOT change length during contraction.
bands.I_band: light band. actin only (thin filaments). SHORTENS during contraction.
bands.H_zone: center of A band. myosin only (no actin overlap). SHORTENS during contraction.

steps: 1. nerve impulse arrives at neuromuscular junction (NMJ)
3. ACh binds receptors → action potential along sarcolemma → into T-tubules
4. T-tubules signal sarcoplasmic reticulum (SR) → releases Ca2+
5. Ca2+ binds troponin → tropomyosin moves → exposes actin binding sites
6. myosin heads bind actin (cross-bridge) → power stroke → ADP+Pi released
7. new ATP binds myosin → cross-bridge detaches → cycle repeats
8. when nerve signal stops → Ca2+ pumped back into SR → tropomyosin re-covers sites → relaxation

key_molecules.actin: thin filament. has binding sites for myosin.
key_molecules.myosin: thick filament. heads do the pulling (power stroke).
key_molecules.tropomyosin: covers actin binding sites at rest.
key_molecules.troponin: regulatory protein. Ca2+ binds to it → moves tropomyosin.
key_molecules.ATP: energy for: power stroke, cross-bridge detaching, Ca2+ pump.
key_molecules.Ca2+: the trigger. no calcium = no contraction.
key_molecules.ACh: neurotransmitter at NMJ. starts the whole chain.

isotonic.concentric: muscle shortens under load. bicep curl UP.
isotonic.eccentric: muscle lengthens under load. bicep curl DOWN. where soreness comes from.

contraction_types.isometric: muscle generates force but doesn't change length. pushing against a wall.

key_topics.motor_unit: one motor neuron + all the muscle fibers it innervates. small motor units = fine control (eyes). large motor units = power (quads).

twitch_summation_tetanus.summation: repeated stimuli before full relaxation → forces add up.

tetanus.incomplete: visible relaxation between stimuli but forces accumulate.
tetanus.complete: no relaxation between stimuli. sustained max contraction.

muscle_fiber_types.slow_oxidative_type1: slow twitch, fatigue-resistant, aerobic, red (myoglobin), marathon runners.
muscle_fiber_types.fast_oxidative_type2a: fast twitch, moderate fatigue resistance, aerobic+anaerobic, middle distance.
muscle_fiber_types.fast_glycolytic_type2b: fast twitch, fatigues quickly, anaerobic, white, sprinters/powerlifters.

energy_systems.immediate: stored ATP + creatine phosphate. first 10-15 seconds.
energy_systems.glycolytic: anaerobic glycolysis. glucose → pyruvate → lactic acid. 30-40 seconds.
energy_systems.oxidative: aerobic respiration. glucose/fatty acids → CO2 + H2O + lots of ATP. sustained activity.

key_topics.rigor_mortis: after death: no ATP → myosin can't detach from actin → muscles lock. resolves when proteins degrade.

major_muscle_groups.head_neck: frontalis, occipitalis, orbicularis oculi, orbicularis oris, masseter, temporalis, sternocleidomastoid, platysma
major_muscle_groups.trunk: pectoralis major/minor, intercostals, diaphragm, rectus abdominis, external/internal obliques, transversus abdominis, erector spinae, latissimus dorsi, trapezius
major_muscle_groups.upper_limb: deltoid, biceps brachii, triceps brachii, brachialis, brachioradialis, flexor/extensor groups of forearm
major_muscle_groups.lower_limb: iliopsoas, gluteus maximus/medius/minimus, quadriceps (rectus femoris, vastus lateralis/medialis/intermedius), hamstrings (biceps femoris, semitendinosus, semimembranosus), tibialis anterior, gastrocnemius, soleus

divisions.PNS: everything else — cranial nerves, spinal nerves, ganglia
divisions.autonomic: involuntary. smooth muscle, cardiac muscle, glands.

neurons.structure: cell body (soma) → dendrites (receive) → axon (transmit) → axon terminals (release NT)
neurons.types_by_structure: multipolar (most common), bipolar (retina, inner ear), unipolar/pseudounipolar (sensory)

CNS.astrocytes: BBB maintenance, support, nutrient transfer. star-shaped. MOST ABUNDANT glial cell.
CNS.oligodendrocytes: myelination in CNS. one cell wraps multiple axons.

PNS.schwann_cells: myelination in PNS. one cell wraps ONE axon segment.
PNS.satellite_cells: surround cell bodies in ganglia. support.

action_potential.resting_potential: -70mV. Na+ outside, K+ inside. maintained by Na+/K+ ATPase pump (3 Na out, 2 K in).
action_potential.depolarization: stimulus → Na+ channels open → Na+ rushes in → membrane goes positive (+30mV).
action_potential.repolarization: Na+ channels close, K+ channels open → K+ rushes out → membrane returns to negative.
action_potential.hyperpolarization: K+ channels slow to close → overshoots past -70mV briefly.

refractory_periods.absolute: no stimulus can trigger another AP. during depolarization.
refractory_periods.relative: stronger-than-normal stimulus CAN trigger AP. during repolarization.

steps: 2. voltage-gated Ca2+ channels open → Ca2+ enters
3. Ca2+ causes synaptic vesicles to fuse with membrane (exocytosis)
5. NT binds receptors on postsynaptic membrane
6. ion channels open → EPSP (excitatory) or IPSP (inhibitory)
7. NT removed by: reuptake, enzymatic degradation, or diffusion

brain_regions.cerebrum: largest part. cerebral cortex (gray matter outside, white matter inside). two hemispheres. lobes: frontal (motor, personality, speech-Broca's), parietal (sensory, spatial), temporal (hearing, memory, speech-Wernicke's), occipital (vision).
brain_regions.diencephalon: thalamus (sensory relay), hypothalamus (homeostasis, hormones, hunger, thirst, temp), epithalamus (pineal gland → melatonin).
brain_regions.brainstem: midbrain (visual/auditory reflexes), pons (relay, breathing), medulla oblongata (vital reflexes: heart rate, breathing, BP, swallowing, vomiting).
brain_regions.cerebellum: coordination, balance, motor learning. 'little brain.' does NOT initiate movement — refines it.

meninges.layers: dura mater (tough outer) → arachnoid mater (web-like middle) → pia mater (delicate inner, hugs brain surface)

key_topics.CSF: produced by choroid plexus in ventricles. circulates through ventricles and subarachnoid space. cushions brain, removes waste.

spinal_cord.structure: gray matter inside (butterfly/H shape), white matter outside (opposite of brain).
spinal_cord.tracts: ascending = sensory (up to brain). descending = motor (down from brain).
spinal_cord.reflexes: reflex arc: receptor → sensory neuron → integration center (spinal cord) → motor neuron → effector.

cranial_nerves.mnemonic: Oh Oh Oh To Touch And Feel Very Good Velvet AH — Olfactory, Optic, Oculomotor, Trochlear, Trigeminal, Abducens, Facial, Vestibulocochlear, Glossopharyngeal, Vagus, Accessory, Hypoglossal
cranial_nerves.sensory_motor_both: Some Say Marry Money But My Brother Says Big Brains Matter More — S=Sensory, M=Motor, B=Both

sympathetic.effect: fight or flight. dilates pupils, increases HR, dilates bronchioles, inhibits digestion, releases glucose.

parasympathetic.effect: rest and digest. constricts pupils, decreases HR, constricts bronchioles, stimulates digestion.

ch14.title: Endocrine System
ch14.status: upcoming — may be end of A&P 1 or start of A&P 2 depending on school

glands_and_hormones.anterior_pituitary: GH, TSH, ACTH, FSH, LH, PRL. 'master gland' (controlled by hypothalamus).
glands_and_hormones.posterior_pituitary: stores/releases oxytocin and ADH (made in hypothalamus).
glands_and_hormones.parathyroid: PTH (raises blood Ca2+ — opposite of calcitonin).
glands_and_hormones.adrenal_cortex: cortisol (stress, anti-inflammatory), aldosterone (Na+ retention, BP), androgens.
glands_and_hormones.pancreas: insulin (lowers blood glucose — beta cells), glucagon (raises blood glucose — alpha cells).

hormone_types.water_soluble: amino acid-based. bind surface receptors → second messenger (cAMP). fast, short-lived.
hormone_types.lipid_soluble: steroids. cross membrane → bind intracellular receptors → alter gene expression. slow, long-lasting.

feedback_loops.negative: most common. output inhibits input. thermostat model. e.g., high T3/T4 → inhibits TSH release.
feedback_loops.positive: rare. output amplifies input. e.g., oxytocin during labor, blood clotting cascade.
